title: How do we find the most popular game in our own class?
description: A question from the book asks you to find the most popular game among your own classmates. The video runs the same plan on a new class: ask everyone, group the answers, count each group and pick the largest.
teaching_notes: One idea: the plan of the solved example works on any class, but the answer depends on the classmates. Watch for children who forget to ask every classmate, or forget that two games can tie.

source: Figure it Out: find the most popular game among your classmates
video_script.why: The child carries the whole plan of collecting and counting over to their own class.
video_script.substitution: none: the question asks for the child's own class, so no numbers are fixed
video_script.anchor: your own classmates and their favourite games
video_script.payoff_line: The most popular game is the one with the largest count in your own class.

final_answer.value: the game with the largest count in your own class
final_answer.spoken: the game with the largest count in your own class

hold_back: largest count in your own class
maths_rules: No count is fixed: the answer depends on the class survey.
If two games have the same largest count, both are the most popular.
